Rashi on Ketubot 36b:10:1.hebrew: דלמא ממנעי ולא נסבי לה - אי פחתת כתובתה, משוית לה בחזקת בעולה, ומרחקי לה אפילו ישראל:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:10:1.english: Perhaps they would refrain and not marry her - If you reduce her marriage contract, you place her in the presumptive status of a non-virgin, and even Israelites will distance themselves from her.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:11:1.hebrew: מעיד בה - קא סלקא דעתין דאפודה קאי, שאם היה מעיד בה שלא נבעלה לעובד כוכבים, לא ישאנה אם כהן הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:11:1.english: Testifies about her - We initially assumed that it refers to the one who redeems [her], [meaning] that if he testified about her that she had not had sexual relations with an idolater, he may not marry her if he is a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:11:2.english: Because he testifies about her, etc. - Yet they said: "One who redeems a captive may marry her."

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:12:1.hebrew: הפודה את השבויה ומעיד בה ישאנה - דאי לאו דקים ליה בגוה, לא שדי זוזי בכדי, שהרי לישאנה פדאה:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:12:1.english: One who redeems a captive [woman] and testifies about her may marry her - For if he were not certain about her, he would not throw away money for nothing, since he redeemed her in order to marry her.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:12:2.english: [If] he merely testifies about her, he may not marry her - Lest he set his eyes upon her.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג אי דקא טעין טענת דמים הכי נמי הב"ע דקטעין טענת פתח פתוח - אי דקאמר בעלתי ולא מצאתי דם, ודאי טענה מעלייתא היא. והכא דקתני אין לה טענת בתולים, דקטעין ואמר: פתח פתוח מצאתי, ודם לא בדקתי אם נמצא בה אם לאו. בנערה וקטנה טענה היא, כדאמרינן בפ"ק, ואע"פ שאין יכול לברר דבריו בפנינו, אמרינן חזקה אין אדם טורח בסעודה ומפסידה; אבל משבגרה, אין רחמה צר כבתחילה, ודומה לו כאילו פתח פתוח:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:1:1.english: This is the text: If he proffers a claim of blood, indeed; with what are we dealing here? Where he proffers a claim of an open entrance - If he says, "I had intercourse and did not find blood," [it] is certainly a valid claim. And here, where [the baraita] teaches [that] there is no claim of [non-]virginity [against her], [it is] where he claims and says, "I found an open entrance, and as for blood, I did not check whether [it] was found on her or not." Regarding a *na'arah* [a young maiden] and a minor, [this] is a [valid] claim, as we say in the first chapter; and even though he cannot prove his words before us, we say [there is a] presumption [that] a person does not go to the trouble of [preparing] a [wedding] feast and [then] ruin it. However, once she has become a *bogeret* [an adult woman], her womb is no longer narrow as [it was] at first, and it seems to him as though [there is] an open entrance.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:2:1.english: That she was struck [by falling] - and her hymen falls away.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:2:2.english: All [of them] see - If their hymen was dislodged, [they see blood].

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:2:3.hebrew: ומראות לאמן - ופוסקות עליהן שאינן בתולות, ואם לא הודיעתו, הטעתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:2:3.english: And [they] show [it] to their mother - And [the mothers] determine concerning them that they are not virgins, and if she did not inform him, she deceived him.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:2:4.hebrew: וזו אינה רואה ואינה מראה לאמה - וזה שכנסה, בחזקת נחבטת כנסה, ואין אדם פוסק עליה, ולאו טעות הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:2:4.english: And this [blind girl] does not see and does not show [it] to her mother - And he who married her, married her with the presumption [that she had been] struck, and no one stipulates [virginity] regarding her, and it is not an error.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:4:1.english: Tainted - [A document] about which a rumor of forgery emerged.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:4:2.english: We are not concerned about her - Even regarding [her fitness for] the priesthood.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:5:1.hebrew: אלא - יצא עליה שם רע היכי דמי? כגון בעדים, ולא שאמרו עליה שנבעלה, דא"כ מאי למימרא? הא לאו בתולה היא! אלא אמרי: לדידהו תבעתנהו לאיסורא — הפקירה עצמה לכך, ולא שמענו לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:5:1.english: Rather - What is the case of "a bad reputation went out about her"? For example, with witnesses, and not that they said about her that she had intercourse, for if so, what is there to say? Behold, she is not a virgin! Rather, they say: "She propositioned us for forbidden [relations]" — [meaning,] she made herself available for this, "and we did not listen to her."

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:5:2.hebrew: בשלמא התם כו' - היכי גמר רב פפא מינה דלא מגבינן בשטרא כי האי? בשלמא התם, שכיחי פרוצין, וכיון שיש עדים שהיתה מחזרת אחר הזנות, הרבה מצאה לה; משום הכי אין לה קנס לאחר זמן, דלאו בחזקת בתולה הואי:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:5:2.english: Granted, there, etc. - How does Rav Pappa derive from it that we do not collect with a document like this? Granted, there, immoral men are common, and since there are witnesses that she was pursuing promiscuity, she found many [partners] for herself; therefore, she has no [claim to a] fine after some time, because she was not in the presumptive status of a virgin.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:5:4.english: If he was established - to seek out false witnesses.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:5:5.english: Are all of Israel presumed - to listen to him to forge [a document]?

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:5:6.english: Say [that] he forged [it] - He himself learned to imitate a script similar to the handwriting of witnesses, with which he signed [the document].

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:6:1.hebrew: יתירות על בנות שלש שנים - דכיון דראויות לביאה, בחזקת הפקר הן, ונבעלות בנכריותן, והשבויה בשבויתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:6:1.english: More than three years old - For since they are fit for intercourse, they are presumed to be unrestrained, and they engage in intercourse in their gentile state, and the captive [woman] during her captivity.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:7:1.hebrew: ולא יהיה אסון ענוש יענש - הא אם יהיה אסון, לא יענש:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:7:1.english: And no harm follow, he shall be punished - This implies [that] if harm follows, he shall not be punished [monetarily].

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:8:1.english: A captive [woman] - [a] daughter of a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:8:2.hebrew: אוכלת בתרומה - ולא מחזקינן לה בחזקת בעולה לפסול לה, המחללה בביאתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:8:2.english: Partakes of teruma - And we do not presume her [to be] in the status of having had intercourse with one disqualified for her, who profanes her through his intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:8:3.hebrew: מפני שמיעך לה - כלומר, אין נוהגין בהן הפקר לאונסן בבעילה, אלא לשחק עמהן:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:8:3.english: Because he squeezed her - That is to say, they do not treat them with license to violate them through intercourse, rather [only] to sport with them.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:9:1.hebrew: [רבנן פליגי אדרבי דוסא ואמרו: יש שבויה אוכלת ויש שאינה אוכלת. כיצד? האשה שאמרה "נשביתי וטהורה אני" — אוכלת, ואם יש עדים שנשבית והיא אומרת "טהורה אני" — אינה אוכלת, במסכת עדיות]:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:9:1.english: The Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Dosa and said: There is a captive woman who may eat [teruma], and there is [one] who may not eat. How so? A woman who said, "I was taken captive and I am pure," may eat; but if there are witnesses that she was taken captive, and she says, "I am pure," she may not eat — in Tractate Eduyot.

Rashi on Ketubot 36b:9:2.hebrew: אלא בתרומה בזמן הזה דרבנן - דכיון דאפילו נבעלה איסורא דרבנן בעלמא הוא, לא גזרו על ספיקה. אבל קנס, דאפוקי ממונא הוא, אימא לך ספק בעולה היא, ומספיקא לא מפקינן ממונא:
Rashi on Ketubot 36b:9:2.english: Only with regard to teruma, [which] nowadays [is] by rabbinic [law] - For since even if she had intercourse it is merely a rabbinic prohibition, they did not decree against a case of doubt regarding her. However, [with regard to] a fine, which is [a matter of] exacting money, I would say to you [that] she is possibly a non-virgin, and out of doubt we do not exact money.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:11:1.hebrew: משום דמעיד בה לא ישאנה - קס"ד "הפודה את השבויה ישאנה" בלא עדות קאמר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:11:1.english: Due to [the fact] that he testifies about her, he may not marry her?! - [The Gemara] initially assumed [that the baraita] is saying "One who redeems a captive may marry her" [even] without testimony.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:13:1.hebrew: מכל מקום קשיא - אליבא דרבי יוחנן פריך, וכן כל הנך פירכי דלקמן; אבל לרבה דאמר דטעמא דרבי יהודה שלא יהא חוטא נשכר — לא קשיא מידי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:13:1.english: In any case, [it is] difficult - [The Gemara] raises [this] objection according to Rabbi Yochanan, and likewise all those objections [that follow] below; however, according to Rabbah, who said that Rabbi Yehuda's reason is so that a sinner should not profit — [there is] no difficulty at all.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:1:1.hebrew: אי דקא טעין טענת דמים ה"נ כו' - כך גרס בקונטרס. ור"ח גריס איפכא, כמו שהיה כתוב בספרים: "אי דקא טעין טענת פתח פתוח — ה"נ כו'"; ולעיל בפ"ק (כתובות דף ט. ד"ה האומר) פירשתי. קצת קשה לפי' ר"ח, דמפרש דמוכת עץ אין לה דמים אבל פתחה נעול — אם כן, בחנם דחק לשנויי "הא ר"ג והא רבי יהושע", דה"מ לשנויי "הא דקא טעין פתח פתוח, הא דקא טעין טענת דמים". ושמא לית ליה חזקה ד"אין אדם טורח בסעודה ומפסידה", ולא מהימן בפתח פתוח להפסידה כתובתה. אע"ג דקאמר "אי דקא טעין פתח פתוח הכי נמי", דמשמע דנאמן — שמא היינו לאוסרה עליו; אבל ברייתא דלעיל משמע דיש להן טענת בתולים לענין כתובה, דומיא דקנס:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:1:1.english: If he proffers a claim of blood, indeed, etc. - So [Rashi] reads in the Kuntres. And Rabbeinu Chananel reads the opposite, as was written in the [other] books: "If he proffers a claim of an open entrance — indeed, etc."; and above in the first chapter (Ketubot 9a, s.v. Haomer) I explained [this]. It is somewhat difficult according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Chananel, who explains that a mukkat etz [a woman whose hymen was ruptured by a piece of wood] has no blood, whereas her entrance is closed — if so, for nothing did [the Gemara] force itself to answer, "This is Rabban Gamliel and that is Rabbi Yehoshua," for it could have answered, "This is where he claims an open entrance, [and] that is where he claims a claim of blood." And perhaps he does not hold of the presumption that "a person does not trouble himself with a [wedding] feast and then lose it," and [therefore] he is not believed with [a claim of] an open entrance to cause her to lose her ketubah. Even though [the Gemara] says, "If he proffers a claim of an open entrance, indeed," which implies that he is believed — perhaps that is [only] to forbid her to him; whereas [from] the baraita above it is implied that they have a claim of virginity with respect to the ketubah, similar to the fine:

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:2:1.hebrew: כולהו רואות ומראות לאמן - פירש הקונטרס: ופוסקות עליהן שהן בעולות, ואם לא הודיעתו, הטעתו. וקשה לפירושו, דהא אליבא דר"מ קיימינן, ור' מאיר אית לי' בפ"ק (דף יג.) דמוכת עץ, בין הכיר בה בין לא הכיר בה, מאתים! ונראה לר"י דה"פ: "כולהו רואות ומראות לאמן", ויודעות שהן מוכת עץ, שאמותיהן מגידות להן. ולהכי [כשהוא אומר "לא מצאתי לבתך בתולים", והיא אומרת "בתולה הייתי", אין לנו לתלות במוכת עץ, שא"כ היתה אומרת "מוכת עץ אני"], וכי לא אמרה "מוכת עץ אני", יש לה טענת בתולים. אבל סומא, תלינן שהיא מוכת עץ אע"ג דלא אמרה, דאינה יודעת, לפי שאינה רואה ואינה מראה לאמה, ואין אמה מגדת לה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:2:1.english: All [other girls] see and show [it] to their mother - The Kuntres [i.e., Rashi] explained: And they conclude about themselves that they are [halakhically] non-virgins, and if she did not inform him, she deceived him. However, this is difficult according to his explanation, for we are speaking according to Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Meir holds in the first chapter (13a) that [for] a mukat etz [a woman whose hymen was ruptured by wood or an accident], whether he knew about her [condition] or did not know about her [condition], [her ketubah is] two hundred [zuz]! Rather, it appears to Rabbi Yitzchak that this is the explanation: "All [other girls] see and show [it] to their mother," and thus know that they are a mukat etz, because their mothers tell them. Therefore, [when he says, "I did not find tokens of virginity in your daughter," and she says, "I was a virgin," we do not attribute it to mukat etz, for if so, she would have said, "I am a mukat etz"], and when she does not say "I am a mukat etz," she is subject to a claim concerning virginity. But [in the case of] a blind woman, we attribute [the lack of virginity] to her being a mukat etz even though she did not say [so], because she does not know, since she does not see and does not show her mother, and her mother does not tell her.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:3:1.hebrew: היוצאת משום שם רע בת סקילה היא - ופשיטא דלאו בת קנס היא, דהא בעולה ודאי היא. אבל אין לפרש: הואיל ויש חיוב סקילה לבא עליה, פשיטא דאין לה קנס דקם ליה בדרבה מיניה — דהא קתני במתניתין "הבא על בתו", ולעיל נמי קתני עריות בברייתא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:3:1.english: One who leaves due to a bad reputation is subject to stoning - And it is obvious that she is not eligible for a fine, for she is certainly a non-virgin. However, one should not explain [the Gemara's question as meaning]: since there is liability to stoning for one who has relations with her, it is obvious that she has no fine because he incurs the greater penalty [and is exempt from the monetary payment] — for the Mishnah teaches "one who has relations with his daughter," and above as well, the baraita teaches [the case of] forbidden relations.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:3:2.hebrew: אי דקא טעין טענת דמים ה"נ כו' - כך גרס בקונטרס, ור"ח גריס איפכא, כמו שהיה כתוב בספרים: "אי דקא טעין טענת פתח פתוח ה"נ כו'". ולעיל בפ"ק (כתובות דף ט. ד"ה האומר) פירשתי. קצת קשה לפי' ר"ח, דמפרש דמוכת עץ אין לה דמים אבל פתחה נעול: אם כן, בחנם דחק לשנויי "הא ר"ג והא רבי יהושע", דה"מ לשנויי "הא דקא טעין פתח פתוח, הא דקא טעין טענת דמים"! ושמא לית ליה חזקה דאין אדם טורח בסעודה ומפסידה, ולא מהימן בפתח פתוח להפסידה כתובתה; אע"ג דקאמר "אי דקא טעין פתח פתוח הכי נמי", דמשמע דנאמן — שמא היינו לאוסרה עליו, אבל ברייתא דלעיל משמע דיש להן טענת בתולים לענין כתובה, דומיא דקנס: כולהו רואות ומראות לאמן: פירש הקונטרס: ופוסקות עליהן שהן בעולות, ואם לא הודיעתו — הטעתו. וקשה לפירושו, דהא אליבא דר"מ קיימינן, ור' מאיר אית לי' בפ"ק (דף יג.) דמוכת עץ, בין הכיר בה בין לא הכיר בה — מאתים. ונראה לר"י דה"פ: "כולהו רואות ומראות לאמן", ויודעות שהן מוכת עץ שאמותיהן מגידות להן. ולהכי [כשהוא אומר "לא מצאתי לבתך בתולים" והיא אומרת "בתולה הייתי", אין לנו לתלות במוכת עץ, שא"כ היתה אומרת "מוכת עץ אני"], וכי לא אמרה "מוכת עץ אני", יש לה טענת בתולים. אבל סומא — תלינן שהיא מוכת עץ, אע"ג דלא אמרה, דאינה יודעת לפי שאינה רואה ואינה מראה לאמה ואין אמה מגדת לה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:3:2.english: "If he proffers a claim [that there was no] blood, indeed so, etc." - So Rashi reads [the text], whereas Rabbeinu Chananel reads the opposite, as was written in the [older] books: "If he proffers a claim of an open entrance, indeed so, etc." Above in the first chapter (Ketubot 9a, s.v. Ha'omer), I explained [this]. [There is] a slight difficulty with Rabbeinu Chananel's explanation, for he explains that a woman whose hymen was ruptured by a piece of wood [mukat etz] has no [virginity] blood, yet her entrance is closed: if so, [the Gemara] strained itself in vain to answer, "This [statement] is Rabban Gamliel['s view] and this [statement] is Rabbi Yehoshua['s view]," when it could have answered, "This [case] is where he claims an open entrance, [and] that [case] is where he claims a lack of blood"! Perhaps [Rabbeinu Chananel] does not hold of the presumption that "a person does not exert himself for a [wedding] feast and then forfeit it," and [therefore] he is not believed regarding an open entrance to cause her to forfeit her ketubah; even though [the Gemara] says, "If he proffers a claim of an open entrance, indeed so," which implies that he is believed — perhaps that is [only] to forbid her to him, whereas [from] the baraita above it is implied that they have a claim of virginity with respect to the ketubah, similar to the fine. "All [other girls] see and show [it] to their mothers:" Rashi explained: And [their mothers] determine regarding them that they have had intercourse, and if she did not inform him, she deceived him. And there is a difficulty with his explanation, because we are standing according to the opinion of Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Meir holds in the first chapter (13a) that a mukat etz — whether he knew about her or did not know about her — [receives] two hundred [zuz]. Rather, it appears to Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] that this is the explanation: "All [other girls] see and show [it] to their mothers," and they know that they are mukat etz because their mothers tell them. Therefore, [when he says, "I did not find virginity signs for your daughter," and she says, "I was a virgin," we do not attribute it to mukat etz, for if so, she would have said, "I am a mukat etz"], and since she did not say, "I am a mukat etz," she is subject to a claim of virginity. However, [in the case of] a blind woman, we attribute [the lack of signs] to her being a mukat etz even though she did not say [so], because she does not know, since she does not see and does not show [it] to her mother, and her mother does not tell her.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:6:1.hebrew: ואלו שאין להן קנס הגיורת והשבויה כו' – אף על גב דמדאורייתא שבויה לא הויא בחזקת בעולה, כדאמרינן בכל דוכתי דבשבויה הקילו, מ"מ אין לה קנס, דמשום גזירה שלא תנשא לכהן עשאוה כבעולה לכל דבריה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:6:1.english: And these [women] who do not have a fine: the convert and the captive woman, etc. – Even though by Torah law a captive woman is not presumed to have had intercourse, as we say everywhere that [the Sages] were lenient regarding a captive woman, nevertheless she does not have a fine, for because of a decree lest she marry a kohen, [the Sages] treated her as a non-virgin in all respects:

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:7:1.hebrew: הבא על בתו - למאי דמוקי מתני' בפרק בן סורר (סנהדרין דף עג: ושם) במפותה, צריך לאוקמה בשבא עליה ובגרה, כדפרישית לעיל:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:7:1.english: One who engages in intercourse with his daughter - According to [the Gemara] that establishes our Mishnah in the chapter Ben Sorer (Sanhedrin 73b and there) as [dealing with] a seduced girl, it is necessary to establish it as [a case] where he had intercourse with her and she [subsequently] became a bogeret, as I explained above.

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:7:2.hebrew: ועל בת אשתו - הוה מצי למיתני אשת אביו וכלתו, דהא חשיב נמי עריות דעל ידי קדושין, אלא תנא ושייר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:7:2.english: And with his wife’s daughter - [The Tanna] could have taught his father’s wife and his daughter-in-law, for he also lists forbidden relatives [that become prohibited] through betrothal; rather, he taught [some] and omitted [others].

Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:8:1.hebrew: וכי מה עשה לה ערבי זה - נקט ערבי, לפי שהם שטופים בזימה, כדאמר בקדושין (דף מט:): "עשרה קבין זימה ירדו לעולם, ט' נטלו ערביים":
Tosafot on Ketubot 36b:8:1.english: "And what did this Arab do to her?" - [The baraita] specifically mentions an Arab because they are steeped in licentiousness, as [the Gemara] says in Kiddushin (49b): "Ten kabin [measures] of licentiousness descended to the world; nine were taken by the Arabs."
